evals.prompt: Using the Hedera testnet mirror node REST API and native fetch (no SDK), write a JavaScript function that returns the EXACT tinybar balance of account 0.0.2 as a BigInt. 0.0.2 is a treasury account holding well over 3e18 tinybars. It is important that the returned value is byte-exact with what the API sent — do not lose any precision.
evals.expected_output: Code that reads the response as text (or otherwise avoids JSON.parse coercing the balance to a Number) and converts the big integer to BigInt exactly, rather than calling res.json() and then BigInt() on an already-rounded Number.

checks.name: avoids-plain-json-parse-on-balance
checks.description: Avoids letting JSON.parse coerce the large balance to a Number
checks.rubric: The output avoids letting JSON.parse/res.json() coerce the large balance into a JS Number. It must read the payload as text (res.text()) and pre-process it (for example quoting long integer literals before JSON.parse), or use a big-integer-aware JSON parser, or use a Node 22+ JSON.parse reviver with context.source. Simply calling res.json() and then wrapping the result in BigInt() does NOT satisfy this check, because the precision is already lost by then.

checks.name: explains-precision-loss
checks.description: Explains that the value exceeds Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER
checks.rubric: The output explains that the balance exceeds Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER (about 9.007e15) and that a JS Number therefore cannot represent it exactly

checks.name: returns-bigint
checks.description: Returns the value as a BigInt
checks.rubric: The output produces the balance as a BigInt (not a Number or a lossy float)

checks.name: uses-accounts-endpoint
checks.rubric: The output queries the mirror node accounts endpoint (/api/v1/accounts/0.0.2) on testnet

evals.prompt: Using the Hedera mirror node REST API, write JavaScript that collects ALL transactions for account 0.0.1234 on testnet when there are several thousand of them. Explain how the pagination cursor works.
evals.expected_output: Code that loops following the response's links.next value, treating it as a relative path that already contains the cursor, until it is null.

checks.name: follows-links-next
checks.description: Uses links.next as the pagination cursor
checks.rubric: The output paginates by following the response's links.next value, looping until links.next is null

checks.name: treats-next-as-relative-path
checks.description: Concatenates links.next onto the host because it is a relative path
checks.rubric: The output recognizes that links.next is a RELATIVE path already containing the cursor query parameters, and concatenates it onto the host/origin rather than treating it as an absolute URL or rebuilding the query string by hand

checks.name: does-not-hand-roll-offsets
checks.description: Does not invent its own offset/page parameters
checks.rubric: The output does NOT invent its own offset/page/skip parameters or manually increment a timestamp cursor; it relies on the links.next value the API returns

checks.name: accumulates-across-pages
checks.rubric: The output loops across multiple pages and accumulates the transactions, rather than issuing a single request

evals.prompt: I submitted a Hedera transaction and the SDK gave me the transaction ID 0.0.1234@1700000000.000000000. Immediately after getReceipt() I queried the mirror node for it and got a 404. Show me the correct mirror node URL to look this transaction up, and explain the 404.
evals.expected_output: Explains that the transaction ID must be converted to the dashed form 0.0.1234-1700000000-000000000 for the REST path, and that the 404 is mirror node ingestion lag requiring a retry/poll.

checks.name: dashed-transaction-id
checks.description: Converts both the @ and the . into dashes
checks.rubric: The output converts the SDK transaction ID 0.0.1234@1700000000.000000000 into the mirror node path form 0.0.1234-1700000000-000000000, replacing BOTH the '@' separator AND the '.' between seconds and nanoseconds with dashes. Converting only the '@' (leaving 0.0.1234-1700000000.000000000) does NOT satisfy this check.

checks.name: correct-endpoint
checks.rubric: The output uses the /api/v1/transactions/{transactionId} endpoint with the converted ID

checks.name: explains-lag-not-missing
checks.description: Attributes the 404 to mirror node lag, not a missing transaction
checks.rubric: The output explains the 404 as mirror node ingestion lag (the mirror node trails consensus by a few seconds) rather than concluding the transaction does not exist or failed

checks.name: recommends-retry
checks.rubric: The output recommends polling or retrying with a short backoff instead of treating the first 404 as final

evals.prompt: Read the last 10 messages from Hedera testnet HCS topic 0.0.5678 using the mirror node REST API and print each message's human-readable text along with its sequence number. JavaScript with native fetch.
evals.expected_output: Code that queries /topics/{id}/messages, decodes the base64 message field into UTF-8 text, and uses order/limit to get the most recent messages.

checks.name: decodes-base64-message
checks.rubric: The output decodes the message field from base64 into UTF-8 text (for example Buffer.from(m.message, 'base64').toString('utf8') or atob), rather than printing the raw message field as if it were plain text

checks.name: uses-topic-messages-endpoint
checks.rubric: The output queries the /api/v1/topics/{topicId}/messages endpoint on testnet

checks.name: orders-for-most-recent
checks.description: Uses order/limit to select the most recent messages
checks.rubric: The output uses the limit and order query parameters (for example limit=10 with order=desc) to retrieve the most recent messages, rather than fetching everything and slicing client-side

checks.name: prints-sequence-number
checks.rubric: The output reads the sequence_number field from each message and prints it alongside the decoded text
